rationale: All 314 pages screened through English OCR with candidate presentation boundaries visually checked and official program titles independently screened. Sweet potato 1P-135 concerns pancreatic insulin, 1P-112 concerns mouse light-off timing, and 2P-307 concerns L-DOPA-related itch. These are distinct contexts. OCR errors remain possible.

The original juvenile parkinsonism case records visual hallucinations with levodopa-related complications. No per-period hallucination count or dried fig exposure. Figure labels and a dried blood-spot specimen explain the lexical pairing.

The original cross-sectional cohort includes 134 Parkinson participants. Table 1 shows pain score 1.5 (SD 3.0) on the NMSS frequency by severity item. Later factor analyses concern a combined symptom construct and have no date-fruit exposure contrast.
The same cohort reports mean Apathy Scale 11.9 (SD 7.7). A factor combines apathy and depression for quality-of-life associations, without an isolated apathy intervention or date-fruit exposure.

The crossover records Parkinson apathy by acute DBS state. The apathy omnibus p=.009 exceeds the declared Bonferroni threshold .005. Dorsal versus stimulation-off difference +7.1 (SD 20.8, nominal p=.006) does not resolve that gate. No dried-date arm.

Oxford cohort apathy item score at least 1 predicts impulse-control behaviors, adjusted OR 2.71 (95% CI 1.34 to 5.52). The apathy item is a predictor rather than a change outcome. No dried-date contrast.
